notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after five searches (the five legislative candidates). Everything else was read by opening pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt obeyed: the candidates' own sites, each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates, the University of Minnesota's election archive and one St. Cloud Live article.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned from a scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) had been run; each was then opened. One more was found: Erin Maye Quade's, reached by trying an address and kept because its own pages name her, the office and her city.

Not read: mncourts.gov and www.co.clearwater.mn.us ask scripts to stay out (robots.txt), so nothing was looked up there for the two judges or the Clearwater County Recorder. Nothing was found, by opening the governments' own pages, for Ann Skoe, Justin Peterson, Rodney C. Knutson, Cole Weick, Brett Lee Olson, Janine Schneider, Darrin Hoverson, Thea Fransen, Nancy Dager, Ann Schultz Counihan, Kerry W. Meyer or Justin Collins; the county, city and district pages that could be read do not list them as holding the office today.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: all 31 addresses were opened again with the kit's honest User-Agent (robots.txt obeyed) and every one answered. 44 findings checked; none removed. Two corrected: Koochiching County's board page gives "Served Since: 2019" for Jason Sjoblom (the 2023 lines belong to the commissioners listed around him); and School District 191's Board of Education page does not name Tyler Sachse as a member in its readable text (it only links the district's news post), so his official page now points at that post. The Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates does not print a year; it is the party's current list and names each candidate with the district sought in 2026. Leslie Larson's campaign site ties her to the Blaine council seat in her own words ("I also serve as your Ward 2 Councilmember", Why I'm Running page).
